summary:
We developed an interactive, AI-powered dashboard that consolidates, normalizes, and synthesizes decades of NASA’s microgravity combustion data from the Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database into actionable fire safety insights.

To solve the challenge of scattered, heterogeneous records, we built an automated ETL pipeline that unifies disparate CSV schemas, reconciles missing or implicit parameters across investigations (like ACME, FLEX, BASS, and Saffire), and links underlying scientific PDF reports. Users can filter experiments by fuel, oxygen concentration, pressure, and hardware to dynamically generate comparative interactive charts alongside an integrated Large Language Model (LLM) interface. Researchers can query the filtered data in natural language to synthesize findings, flag critical hazards, and access cited source documents.

This matters because fire behaves unpredictably in low-gravity, oxygen-enriched habitats planned for the Moon and Mars. Turning thousands of fragmented files into an intuitive research tool accelerates predictive fire modeling, improves spacecraft safety systems, and informs terrestrial fire detection and suppression technologies.
details:
How It Works & What It Does
Our platform transforms fragmented experimental records from NASA’s Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database into a unified, queryable fire-safety intelligence dashboard:
1. Automated Data Unification (ETL): A custom pipeline ingests heterogeneous CSV files across multiple microgravity combustion investigations (such as ACME, FLEX, BASS, Saffire, and SAME), reconciles inconsistent column names, infers missing domain-specific hardware and fuel parameters, handles sparse (NaN) sensor readings, and indexes associated scientific PDF reports.
2. Dynamic Filtering & Interactive Visualization: Users filter experiments by fuel type, oxygen concentration, pressure, or hardware. The system automatically identifies compatible physical metrics for the selected subset and renders interactive multi-line comparison charts, extreme KPI cards, and individual-vs-peer-average benchmarks.
3. Natural Language AI Synthesis: Researchers can ask complex questions in plain English. An integrated Large Language Model (LLM) analyzes the active filtered dataset and linked PDF documentation to generate evidence-backed summaries, flag critical flammability hazards, and provide direct citations to the underlying study files.
Benefits
Eliminates Manual Data Wrangling: Saves aerospace researchers and students hundreds of hours spent downloading, cleaning, and cross-referencing thousands of incompatible spreadsheets.
Prevents Misleading Comparisons: Automatically separates mutually exclusive experimental metrics (e.g., liquid droplet burn rates vs. solid material flame spread) so users only compare physically equivalent parameters.
Traceable & Verifiable AI: Every AI-generated insight is strictly grounded in the user's active data filters and paired with direct links to the original NASA PDF reports.
Intended Impact
As space agencies prepare for long-duration Moon bases, pressurized rovers, and Mars missions—which will operate in reduced-pressure, oxygen-enriched atmospheres—understanding low-gravity fire behavior is critical for crew survival. Our tool accelerates predictive flammability modeling and helps engineers design safer spacecraft materials, smoke detectors, and fire suppression systems, while also supporting terrestrial advances in fine-water-mist extinguishers and firefighter protective gear.
Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used
Programming Language: Python
Web Framework & UI: Streamlit with custom CSS styling (aerospace telemetry theme)
Data Engineering & Analytics: Pandas, NumPy, Regular Expressions (re), and pathlib for automated schema mapping and sparse-data normalization
Interactive Visualization: Plotly (plotly.graph_objects / plotly.express)
AI & Natural Language Processing: Large Language Model (LLM) API integration with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) / contextual prompt synthesis over filtered CSV statistics and PDF metadata
Version Control & Collaboration: Git and GitHub
